title: The Great Retreat: Stop Promotion From the First Rank
summary: Step behind the pawn, then distinguish a checking promotion from a king move or an underpromotion.

nodes.question: How does Rc1 meet the h-pawn without repeating the earlier stalemate trap?
nodes.explanation: From c1 the rook can capture a queen or rook promoted on h1. If Black moves the king or chooses a lesser promotion, White has a checked winning capture in the complete remaining ending.

branches.title: Independent reply: promote to a queen
commentary: Begin after ...h2, with both white a2/b3 pawns and Black b5/b4/h2 retained. Earlier rook maneuvers are outside this selected proof.
Rc1 is the source’s final move. It places the rook behind h1 without capturing the h-pawn prematurely.
h1=Q is an independently supplied promotion. It threatens White but the queen lands on the rook’s first rank.
Rxh1 captures the new queen and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. Black’s king and doubled b-pawns remain, so the outcome is checked rather than assumed.

branches.title: Independent reply: attack the rook with the king
commentary: Test a legal king move instead of assuming the h-pawn must promote immediately.
Rc1 offers first-rank control while retaining all pawns.
Kb2 attacks Rc1. White must move the rook rather than allow a king capture.
Rh1 gets out of the attack and blocks the h-pawn from in front. The rook can collect it when appropriate.
Ka3 is a representative retreat. The full certificate also checks the other legal king moves, captures and promotions.
Kxb5 captures the back doubled pawn and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. This is an actual pawn capture, not removal of a spare pawn to force tablebase coverage.

branches.title: Independent reply: underpromote to a knight
commentary: Test an underpromotion, keeping the actual piece and its different attack pattern.
Rc1 is the source move. The certificate covers queen, rook, bishop and knight promotions separately.
h1=N promotes without a checking line along the first rank. White need not respond as if it were a queen.
Kxb5 is a legal winning pawn capture into seven-piece coverage, even while the new black knight remains on h1. Exact outcome evidence, rather than a material count, confirms White’s win.

exercises.prompt: Is Black forced to promote immediately?
exercises.answer: No. Kb2 and Kxa2 are legal too. The certificate checks those king moves and all four promotions.

exercises.prompt: Why not always take the new piece on h1?
exercises.answer: A queen or rook creates different threats from a knight or bishop. Against the lesser promotions, a checked winning capture on b5 is available too.
